title: Suspected Parkinson's Disease: Recognition and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult recognition of parkinsonism, exclusion of urgent mimics and rapid specialist referral before dopaminergic treatment.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national Parkinson's disease guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Degeneration of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons impairs movement scaling. Bradykinesia combines with rigidity, rest tremor or postural instability. Non-motor autonomic, sleep, mood and cognitive symptoms can precede motor diagnosis. Atypical features may indicate another parkinsonian disorder.
keyMechanisms: Degeneration of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons impairs movement scaling.
Bradykinesia combines with rigidity, rest tremor or postural instability.
Non-motor autonomic, sleep, mood and cognitive symptoms can precede motor diagnosis.
Atypical features may indicate another parkinsonian disorder.

references.title: NICE NG71: Parkinson's disease in adults

symptoms: Slowness, reduced dexterity, shuffling, rest tremor, stiffness, falls, constipation, REM-sleep behaviour, low mood or reduced smell.
physicalSigns: Bradykinesia, rigidity, rest tremor, reduced arm swing, hypomimia and gait/postural abnormality.
redFlags: Acute onset, focal deficit, encephalopathy, severe autonomic collapse or rapidly progressive falls needs urgent alternative-diagnosis assessment.
precipitants: Dopamine-blocking medicines and vascular or neurodegenerative disease can produce parkinsonism.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Temporal relationship to a dopamine-blocking medicine, often with symmetric signs.
Action/postural tremor without bradykinesia or rigidity.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Refer untreated to a specialist with expertise in differential diagnosis.
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal speed, tone, gait and postural stability

clinicalManagement.title: Exclude acute neurological disease
actions: Use an emergency pathway for acute onset, focal deficit, encephalopathy or rapid deterioration.
Record onset, progression, falls, autonomic and cognitive symptoms and medicine exposure.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer before treatment
actions: Refer suspected Parkinson's disease to a specialist with expertise in differential diagnosis.
Do not start dopaminergic treatment solely as a diagnostic test.

clinicalManagement.title: Reduce risk while awaiting assessment
actions: Address falls, driving, swallowing or occupational risk according to symptoms.
Provide an escalation route for rapid deterioration, aspiration, recurrent falls or confusion.

medicationPlan.note: Do not initiate dopaminergic medicine before specialist diagnostic assessment in this recognition pathway.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Tremor, stiffness, slowness, balance or gait disorder suggesting parkinsonism.

teaching.scope: Adult recognition of parkinsonism, exclusion of urgent mimics and rapid specialist referral before dopaminergic treatment.
pitfalls: Using levodopa response as a primary-care diagnostic test.
Missing drug-induced or acute vascular parkinsonism.
keyPoints: Diagnosis is clinical and should be reviewed over time.
Structural imaging is for selected mimics, not routine confirmation.

patientEducation: Explain diagnostic uncertainty and why specialist assessment precedes treatment.
lifestyleAndDiet: Maintain safe activity and falls precautions while awaiting review.
mdtReferrals: Neurology or movement-disorders service; physiotherapy, speech therapy or occupational therapy if urgent functional needs arise.
dischargeCriteria: Not discharged until referral outcome, risk advice and safety-net are documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track specialist assessment and reassess sooner for falls, aspiration, confusion or rapid progression.
